title: KLIMA: Low-latency mixed-signal In-Memory Computing accelerator for solving arbitrary-order Boolean Satisfiability
problem: Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) solving requires exploring vast search spaces, with conventional CPU/GPU approaches suffering from memory bandwidth and latency bottlenecks. KLIMA addresses solving arbitrary-order SAT problems with single-digit nanosecond latency.
method: KLIMA uses mixed-signal in-memory computing (analog logic with digital interfacing) to perform SAT clause evaluation in memory, eliminating von Neumann bottlenecks by computing directly on stored data using current-mode analog circuits that evaluate Boolean expressions faster than digital logic can fetch operands.

title: EOD: Enabling Low Latency GNN Inference via Near-Memory Concatenate Aggregation
problem: Real-time GNN inference for online services requires an inductive setup where the system must first prepare the computational graph and node features before executing inference, with this preparation step dominating end-to-end latency. The neighborhood explosion problem causes exponential growth in memory access and computation as the number of GNN layers increases.
method: EOD co-designs algorithm and hardware to tackle both challenges. On the algorithmic side, it introduces a precomputation method for training nodes that converts exponential neighborhood aggregation to linear complexity, and a concatenated Zero-Value Compression (ZVC) scheme to compact the stored precomputed hidden features. On the hardware side, EOD implements a Near-Memory Processing (NMP) architecture that performs aggregation directly on ZVC-compressed, concatenated feature data without decompressing to host memory, exploiting the high internal memory bandwidth to eliminate the PCIe/host-memory bottleneck during the preparation stage.

title: Prosperity: Accelerating Spiking Neural Networks via Product Sparsity
problem: Existing SNN accelerators exploit bit sparsity (zero-valued spikes) to skip zero multiplications, but this approach leaves substantial redundancy unexploited: non-zero spike patterns that produce structurally identical inner products across matrix rows are recomputed independently, wasting significant compute.
method: Product Sparsity is a new sparsity paradigm that identifies combinatorially similar binary spike patterns across matrix rows: if two rows share identical non-zero positions, their dot products with the same weight vector are identical and only one needs to be computed, with the result reused for the other. Prosperity implements this via a real-time pattern matching engine that groups rows by their spike pattern hash, computes the inner product once per unique pattern, and distributes results to all matching rows. This is applied to both fully-connected and convolutional layers of SNNs with binary activations.

title: 37.8 A 13.5µW 35-Keyword End-to-End Keyword Spotting System Featuring Personalized On-Chip Training in 28nm CMOS
problem: Existing keyword spotting systems recognize only up to 10 keywords with low accuracy for accented speakers, and lack user-specific trainability, limiting personalization for diverse speech patterns and larger vocabularies.
method: The system employs a compact CNN with on-chip training capability, featuring a sine-based convolution with approximate logarithm function as a low-complexity feature extractor. Training occurs on-chip to adapt to individual users, enabling personalization without external servers while maintaining power efficiency through compact architecture and quantized operations.

title: Comprehensive Placement and Routing Framework with Guaranteed In-Cell Routability for Synthesizing Complementary-FET Cells
problem: CFET cell layout synthesis faces extreme routing resource scarcity due to vertical transistor stacking; existing generators struggle with in-cell routability and produce suboptimal or infeasible layouts.
method: Three-stage approach: (1) partitioning + quality maintenance for scalability, (2) SMT-based placement with partial routing integration to determine pin positions and ensure routability, (3) progressive metal routing using manual-inspired M0 + ILP-based M1/M2 layers to handle unidirectional constraints.

title: AMD Pensando Pollara 400 AI NIC Architecture and Application
problem: Enterprise AI data centers require programmable network interfaces for flexible packet processing, load balancing, and security; Pollara 400 addresses these needs with a programmable SmartNIC targeting 400Gbps throughput.
method: Pollara 400 integrates a programmable packet processing engine (likely PISA-style) with multiple compute cores, high-speed memory hierarchies, and advanced switching fabric to enable in-NIC compute offloads and flexible traffic management.

title: A 10.5mW Automotive Touch AFE IC Featuring Radiated EMI Reduction Based on Pipelined Dual-Frequency Modulation and Sine2 Waveform Shaping for CISPR 25 Class 5 Compliance
problem: Automotive touch-screen sensors must comply with CISPR 25 EMI standards while maintaining high SNR and frame rate, but typical driving signals (200-500kHz) radiate harmonics that violate emission limits; prior approaches (COM, high-voltage, PRP, FDM) either require FFT overhead or are ineffective at attenuating harmonics.
method: Pipelined dual-frequency modulation combined with sine2 waveform shaping in the AFE to reduce radiated EMI without FFT overhead; selective driving signal modulation attenuates harmonics while maintaining SNR and frame rate performance.

title: ELF: Efficient Logic Synthesis by Pruning Redundancy in Refactoring
problem: Logic optimization via refactoring incurs high computational cost; conventional cut-based refactoring fails to improve circuit 98% of the time on average, wasting computation.
method: ELF uses a machine-learning classifier to preemptively prune unsuccessful cut candidates before expensive resynthesis operations. Classifier predicts which cuts are unlikely to yield improvements, eliminating wasted computation. Applies to ABC logic synthesis framework's refactor operator.

title: Predicting DRAM-Caused Risky VMs in Large-Scale Clouds
problem: DRAM failures in large-scale clouds are currently mitigated at node granularity, requiring migration of all VMs on a node even when errors affect only a small fraction of the memory address space. This coarse-grained approach consumes excessive resources and causes unnecessary VM disruptions.
method: Pegasus introduces an Error-VM mapping framework that correlates DRAM ECC error addresses to specific VM memory regions using address space management metadata. A predictor combines ECC correction event features with spatio-temporal clustering features to identify VMs whose working sets overlap with DRAM regions exhibiting uncorrectable error risk. The system operates at VM granularity rather than DIMM/node granularity, enabling selective migration of only at-risk VMs.

title: HyperHammer: Breaking Free from KVM-Enforced Isolation
problem: Existing Rowhammer attacks against virtualized cloud environments can compromise co-resident VMs but have not demonstrated the ability to attack the hypervisor itself, and a key primitive enabling such attacks (double-sided hammering or similar) has been disabled by hypervisor mitigations. This paper develops a new Rowhammer attack capable of breaking KVM-enforced isolation to compromise the hypervisor from a guest VM.
method: HyperHammer constructs a new Rowhammer attack path from within a KVM guest VM that circumvents existing KVM-level mitigations. The attack likely leverages alternative hammering primitives or physical memory addressing techniques (e.g., virtual-to-physical mapping exploitation, huge-page-based addressing) to induce bit flips in hypervisor memory regions, enabling privilege escalation from guest to hypervisor level.

title: FT-MUX: A Fault-Tolerant Microfluidic Multiplexer Design
problem: Microfluidic multiplexers enable routing through many flow channels with few control channels, but as integration scales up, control-channel defects affect large numbers of flow channels, creating reliability concerns.
method: FT-MUX formally analyzes design rules for multiplexers tolerating n defective control channels. Models fault-tolerant MUX design as binary constant weight code (BWCC) problem to minimize resource overhead while maintaining functionality. Determines conditions under which FT-MUX can address more flow channels than standard MUX with equal or fewer control channels.

title: Harmonia: A Unified Framework for Heterogeneous FPGA Acceleration in the Cloud
problem: The shell-role FPGA architecture adopted by cloud providers works well for homogeneous FPGA servers but fails to handle heterogeneous FPGA configurations: prior solutions either require laborious shell development for each FPGA variant (provider burden) or ad-hoc software modifications for each application (user burden), with no portable abstraction across diverse cloud FPGA types.
method: Harmonia introduces a unified framework that abstracts cloud FPGA heterogeneity at both the hardware and software levels. On the hardware side, it defines a standardized shell interface specification that decouples platform-specific shell logic from portable role logic, allowing roles (user accelerators) to be written once and ported across heterogeneous FPGAs. On the software side, Harmonia provides a resource management layer and a driver abstraction that hides FPGA-specific differences from user applications, enabling portability without per-FPGA software modifications.

title: PartIR: Composing SPMD Partitioning Strategies for Machine Learning
problem: Training large neural networks requires combining multiple parallelization strategies (data, model, and optimizer sharding), but existing systems make it difficult to compose, verify, and reason about these strategies in a predictable way. The tight coupling of partitioning strategies with ML implementation code makes it hard to experiment with or automatically derive optimal sharding plans.
method: PartIR provides a schedule-like API that incrementally rewrites a neural network's intermediate representation (IR) after each applied partitioning strategy. Each strategy (data parallelism, tensor/model parallelism, optimizer sharding) is expressed as a composable, declarative transformation on the IR. The system is hardware-and-runtime agnostic and follows well-defined general rewriting rules so each step is independently verifiable. Simulators and users can check the strategy's effect after each incremental rewrite.

title: 28.2 A 189.3dB-FoMs 14.5fJ/Conversion-Step Continuous-Time Noise-Shaping SAR Capacitance-to-Digital Converter
problem: High-resolution capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) for IoT environmental monitoring (humidity, pressure) face kT/C and flicker noise limits. ΔΣM-based CDCs offer high resolution via oversampling/noise-shaping but power consumption remains limited by noise floor.
method: Continuous-time ΔΣM-based CDC using noise-shaping to achieve high resolution while oversampling, directly working in capacitance domain. CT architecture avoids sampling-clock jitter and enables continuous signal processing.

title: OutlierCIM: Outlier-Aware Digital CIM-Based LLM Accelerator with Hybrid-Strategy Quantization and Unified FP-INT Computation
problem: Activation outliers in LLMs (rare large-magnitude values) introduce quantization challenges that degrade model accuracy and efficiency when accelerated in low-bit-width CIM arrays; existing outlier-aware methods struggle to balance accuracy and hardware efficiency.
method: OutlierCIM proposes: (1) outlier-clustered tiling that groups outliers to optimize memory access and workload distribution in CIM arrays, (2) hybrid-strategy quantization with reconfigurable double-bit CIM macro arrays to overcome low storage utilization and latency penalties, and (3) dedicated quantizer and post-processing to unify FP-INT multiplication/accumulation operations caused by outlier handling.

title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Tiling Sparse Tensor Algebra
problem: Tiling sparse tensor algebra computations for cache efficiency is challenging because the effective tile size and cache behavior depend on the sparse data distribution, which varies across inputs and is not known at compile time.
method: The paper takes a probabilistic approach to sparse tensor tiling, modeling the sparsity pattern probabilistically to predict cache behavior and guide tile-size selection. Specific mechanism details are not available from the abstract alone.
